end.summary:
Harsh identified quadrants from the signs of x and y in several examples.
They placed a point on the negative y-axis but questioned whether it also belonged to a quadrant.
They described reflection in the x-axis as keeping x unchanged and changing the sign of y.
They first treated (3, 2) and (2, 3) as the same point, then stated the correct distinction using right/up steps; teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Asha practised identifying quadrants, placing points on axes, reflecting points, and distinguishing ordered pairs. Harsh used the sign pattern correctly in several quadrant examples and described x-axis reflection with the correct rule. They mixed up points on an axis with quadrants and initially treated (3, 2) and (2, 3) as the same; they later explained why those two points are different, but this was not fully secured in the teach-back. At home, ask Harsh to draw the four quadrants and label two points on each axis, noting that axis points are not in any quadrant.
